text:
maria: Heads-up — noticed p99 tokens/sec on the Token-Level SLO dashboard in us-east1 jumped above SLO around 02:30 UTC and is still elevated. Small models (distil-*, micro-*-quant) are the worst hit. Not tied to traffic surge in the ingress logs. Anyone seeing related infra churn?

jon: Looking now. Which dashboard/panel?

maria: Dashboard: "Token-Level SLOs / Live / p99 by model" (dash id 1023). Panel: p99 tokens/sec (grouped by model, region).

grafana-bot: Alert fired: token_slo_p99_us_east1 (firing for 14m). Alert rule: tokensec_p99_alert > 1200 (3m).

sasha: Can you paste the prom query you're using for the panel? I want to check buckets.

jon: The panel uses this (approx):

```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_processing_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, region))
```

jon: I'll run a breakdown by shard_id and instance to see if it's localized.

ethan: FYI I saw a flurry of pod reschedules on the serving pool in us-east1 around 02:25. Autoscaler bumped nodes, then several shards moved. KV cache miss rate spiked in logs.

maria: That matches — bucket-level tail latency sensitive to KV cache cold misses. If shard placement caused caches to flush, p99 for small models (which hit cache a lot) would spike.

sasha: Quick adhoc queries:
```
sum by (shard_id) (rate(kv_cache_miss_total[10m]))
```
and
```
sum by (instance) (rate(container_restarts_total[15m]))
```
showed high misses on shard_id=shard-7 and container restarts on node-gpu-12.

jon: Confirmed. shard-7 accounts for ~55% of the p99 increase for distil-* models. Looks like noisy neighbor during node drain.

maria: Two action threads then: short-term — silence or raise alert threshold for p99 in us-east1 while oncall mitigates; medium — reduce shard churn or pin hot shards during autoscale windows; long-term — add a recording rule that aggregates by stable shard placement and expose "kv_cache_hit_ratio by shard" panel.

oncall-bot: @oncall paging paged oncall (ethan).

ethan: Oncall here. I'll do a temporary alert suppression on token_slo_p99_us_east1 for 30m while we stabilize. Also will cordon node-gpu-12 and migrate shard-7 off noisy host.

sasha: I'll prepare the prometheus recording rule change we discussed yesterday — precompute per-shard histogram sums so dashboards use recording rules instead of expensive cross-series calculations. Proposed rule (draft):
```
- record: token_processing_seconds_bucket:shard:sum_rate
  expr: sum by (le, model, shard_id) (rate(token_processing_seconds_bucket[5m]))
```
Then panel query can be:
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, model) (token_processing_seconds_bucket:shard:sum_rate))
```
This should keep cardinality lower at query time and make p99 stable.

jon: Also we should avoid grouping by instance in the panel; it exploded cardinality when some labels are null. Maybe add `label_replace` to sanitize.

maria: Good. Can we also add a cheap panel showing `kv_cache_miss_rate / kv_cache_request_rate` by shard to quickly spot cold caches? Label it: "Token cache health (by shard)".

ethan: On it. I'll also add a Grafana annotation where the node autoscaler event happened (k8s.event: NodeScaledUp node-gpu-pool). That will help future triage.

sasha: FYI cost note — if we lower p99 alert sensitivity and let the noisy window slide, tokens/sec SLO violations still count toward reports. We should capture the impact in the token-econ dashboard (dash id 1101) — spike in tokens/sec p99 increases per-token cost.

maria: Good point. Add a follow-up: correlate with per-route token split, if small models are serving many short queries, cost impact can be disproportionate.

ethan: Done temporarily: suppressed alert for 30m, cordoned node-gpu-12, migrated shard-7. Re-checking metrics.

jon: After migration, kv_cache_miss_total for shard-7 dropped to baseline in ~7min. p99 trending down but a couple of short spikes remain — likely still warming.

maria: Can we add a runbook link on the alert with steps: check pod reschedules, identify shard_id high miss, cordon/migrate node, and consider recording rule rollback? Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/token-slo-coldstart

sasha: I'll open a ticket to land the recording rule and add shard-level cache panel. TODOs:
- Sasha: implement recording rule PR and tests
- Ethan: follow up on why autoscaler drained node-gpu-12 (cloud provider events)
- Jon: add sanitized label_replace to dashboard queries
- Maria: update alert to reference runbook and set proper for=10m instead of 3m

maria: Thanks — summary: root cause: shard movement + KV cache cold misses caused tokens/sec p99 spikes; mitigated by migrating shard and temporary suppress; engineering follow-ups created.

jon: I'll post a short blip to #incidents with the summary and link to grafana zoom.

grafana-bot: Annotation added to dash 1023 at 1745123400: "shard-7 migration, temporary alert suppression".

ethan: All green for now. Leaving this thread open for the PR review.

maria: Closing once recording rule PR merges and dashboards updated. :thumbsup:
